issues.legal_issue: A letter of award issued during a tender process does not create a binding contract or make a draft agreement’s arbitration clause operative where the tender documents contemplate further steps and execution of a formal agreement before the contract comes into existence.
material_facts: The tender documents disclaimed that they constituted an agreement and described a bidding process that continued after the letter of award.
The letter of award contemplated that a special-purpose entity would be formed and that a concession agreement would be signed later.
The consortium’s proposed change to a single bidder was not approved, the letter of award was withdrawn, and no concession agreement was executed.
The authority nevertheless invoked the draft concession agreement’s arbitration clause to pursue its claim against the bidders.
issues.conclusion: There was no concluded contract between the parties at the letter-of-award stage, and the arbitration clause in the draft concession agreement did not bind them. The order rejecting the arbitration clause’s application was reinstated.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 7 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, acceptance must be absolute and unqualified to convert a proposal into a promise. A prelude to a contract is not the contract itself, and an arbitration clause intended to operate upon a future contract does not become operative if that contract is never made. The Court relied on Dresser Rand S.A. v. Bindal Agro Chem Ltd. (2006) 1 SCC 751 and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd. v. Telephone Cables Ltd. (2010) 5 SCC 213; it distinguished Unissi (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (2009) 1 SCC 107, and applied the qualification in Kollipara Sriramulu v. T. Aswatha Narayana (1968) 3 SCR 387 that parties may intend not to be bound until a formal contract is signed. Section 7(5) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 was also referred to in the arbitrator’s consideration of incorporation by reference.

rule.if: arbitration_jurisdiction_challenge and tender_bid_dispute and documents_disclaim_present_contract and award_requires_later_formal_agreement and formal_agreement_not_executed

predicates.arbitration_jurisdiction_challenge: A party challenges whether an arbitration agreement governs the dispute.
predicates.tender_bid_dispute: The dispute arises during a tender or bidding process, before performance of the proposed contract.
predicates.documents_disclaim_present_contract: The tender documents state that they do not themselves constitute a present contract between the participants.
predicates.award_requires_later_formal_agreement: The award documents contemplate that the parties must take further steps and execute a formal agreement before the proposed contract is made.
predicates.formal_agreement_not_executed: The contemplated formal agreement was not executed.

issues.definition: When an arbitration-jurisdiction challenge concerns a tender-stage dispute, the documents disclaim a present contract, the award requires a later formal agreement, and that agreement is never executed, the bidders are not bound by the proposed contract’s arbitration clause.

issues.legal_issue: A draft arbitration clause for disputes under a future concession agreement does not govern a tender-stage dispute between parties who are not the parties to that concession agreement.
material_facts: The draft arbitration clause applied to disputes connected with the concession agreement between the authority and the concessionaire.
The dispute concerned the bidding process and the withdrawal of the letter of award, before any concession agreement was executed.
The proposed concessionaire was to be a special-purpose entity, while the arbitration was invoked against the consortium members.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming that the arbitration clause had otherwise been incorporated, it was inapt to cover this dispute because it concerned a future concession agreement and different contracting parties.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle concerning the scope and incorporation of arbitration clauses discussed in M.R. Engineers and Contractors Pvt. Ltd. v. Som Datt Builders Ltd. (2009) 7 SCC 696. The clause must govern the particular dispute and the parties to it; a clause directed to disputes under a future contract between different parties does not extend to a tender-stage dispute between bidders and the authority.

predicates.arbitration_jurisdiction_challenge: A party challenges whether an arbitration clause governs the dispute.
predicates.arbitration_clause_limited_to_future_con: The clause applies to disputes arising under or connected with a proposed future contract.
predicates.tender_bid_dispute: The dispute arises from the tender process before the proposed contract is executed.
predicates.dispute_parties_differ_from_future_contr: The parties to the dispute are not the same as the parties identified for the proposed future contract.

issues.definition: A clause limited to disputes under a future contract does not cover a tender-stage dispute when the dispute’s parties differ from the parties to that future contract.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court should not decline to exercise its appellate discretion merely because a party alleges financial loss from a later tender when the challenged judgment incorrectly treats a letter of award as a concluded contract.
material_facts: The appeal was brought under Article 136 of the Constitution against a High Court decision treating the acknowledged letter of award as a binding contract.
The authority relied on an alleged reduction in its revenue share under a later tender as a reason not to interfere.
The appellant contended that the later tender had different conditions and that its bid had been the best among the bids received.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the request not to interfere, held the High Court’s conclusion on contract formation to be incorrect, set aside its judgment, and reinstated the arbitrator’s order.
issues.legal_principle: Article 136 of the Constitution of India confers discretionary appellate jurisdiction. The Court held on these facts that the alleged financial consequences of a later tender did not justify leaving in place a judgment that wrongly treated the letter of award as a concluded contract.

predicates.appeal_under_article_136: A party brings an appeal invoking the Supreme Court’s discretionary appellate jurisdiction.
predicates.high_court_treated_award_as_concluded_co: The High Court treated a letter of award as creating a concluded contract despite further contractual steps remaining.
predicates.later_tender_loss_alleged: A party opposing appellate interference alleges that a later tender caused it financial loss.

issues.definition: When an appeal invokes discretionary appellate jurisdiction, the High Court treated an award as a concluded contract despite further steps remaining, and a party alleges loss from a later tender, the Supreme Court interferes with the High Court judgment.
